question.prompt: Inside a right circular cone with base radius \(5\) and height \(12\) are three congruent spheres each with radius \(r.\) Each sphere is tangent to the other two spheres and also tangent to the base and side of the cone. What is \(r?\)

solutions.explanation:
First relate the three sphere centers, then use a cross-section of the cone. All centers are height \(r\) above the base, because the spheres touch the base. Mutual tangency makes their pairwise distances \(2r\), so they form an equilateral triangle of side \(2r\).

By rotational symmetry of the cone, congruent spheres tangent to its base and side have their centers the same horizontal distance from its axis. The axis therefore passes through the circumcenter of that equilateral triangle. Its altitude is \(r\sqrt3\), so the horizontal distance from the axis to each center is \((2/3)r\sqrt3=2r/\sqrt3\).

Use the cross-section in [Figure 1](figures/2021_Fall_AMC_10A_Q22_official_solution_fig1.png). Let \(C\) be the base center, \(V\) the cone vertex, \(A\) a sphere center, \(B\) its base tangency point, and \(D\) the base boundary point on ray \(CB\). Thus \(AB=r\), \(BC=2r/\sqrt3\), \(CD=5\), and \(CV=12\). The cone's slant length is \(DV=13\) by the Pythagorean Theorem.

The center \(A\) is equally distant from lines \(DC\) and \(DV\), so \(DA\) bisects their angle. Extend \(DA\) to meet \(CV\) at \(E\). The Angle Bisector Theorem in triangle \(DCV\) gives
\[
\frac{CE}{12-CE}=\frac5{13},\qquad CE=\frac{10}{3}.
\]
Right triangles \(DAB\) and \(DEC\) are similar, so
\[
\frac{DB}{5}=\frac r{10/3},\qquad DB=\frac32r.
\]
Finally \(BC+BD=CD\), hence
\[
\frac{2r}{\sqrt3}+\frac32r=5,\qquad
r=\frac{10\sqrt3}{3\sqrt3+4}=\boxed{\frac{90-40\sqrt3}{11}},
\]
choice B.
solutions.title: Use sphere-center geometry and a cone cross-section angle bisector
Similar triangles in a cone section
